name: Marios Pittas
headline: Product design, from first sketch to shipped code.
intro: I'm Marios, a UI/UX and product designer in Bulgaria. Ten years on the web, six of them shipping React, mean my designs are specific about states, edge cases and handoff.
availability: Open to product design roles, remote or hybrid

stats.label: Startup design projects as a UI designer

capabilities.title: Product and UX
capabilities.body: Problem framing, user flows, information architecture and wireframes. I write down who it is for and what success looks like before I open Figma.

capabilities.title: UI and visual design
capabilities.body: Type, layout, colour and motion that hold up at every state, not only on the hero screen. Empty, loading, error and edge cases are part of the design.

capabilities.title: Design systems
capabilities.body: Tokens, components and documentation that designers and developers both use. I have built on MUI and Ant Design and worked with Storybook.

capabilities.title: Design to code
capabilities.body: React, Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind. I prototype in code when a flow needs real behaviour, and I review builds against the design before they ship.

process.title: Understand
process.body: Who is this for, what are they trying to do, and what does the business need? I write it down first.

process.title: Frame
process.body: One clear problem statement, a few design principles and a definition of success the team can check.

process.title: Explore
process.body: Flows first, then low-fidelity options, then the one worth polishing. I keep the rejected options and the reasons.

process.title: Validate
process.body: Real users where possible, teammates where not. Clickable prototypes beat slide decks.

process.title: Ship
process.body: Specs that cover the unhappy states, and I stay in the build through review and QA.

aboutSub: A designer who can also build, and a builder who cares how it feels.
aboutParagraphs: I started in 2016 turning PSD files into responsive websites. After two years I moved into UI design for startups, where I designed web interfaces and brand assets for crypto and early-stage clients.

Since 2020 I have been building production interfaces in React and TypeScript, working from other designers' Figma files. That side of the job taught me what makes a design easy or painful to build: missing states, vague spacing, components that only work in one place.

Now I want to design the products themselves. Outside client work I design and build complete products, like a day planner, a music rating app and an AI training tool for GeoGuessr players, so I know the whole path from the first problem statement to a live URL.
